records.rationale: A singularity of an unspecified coupling does not by itself establish a bifurcation of the solution set or identify that coupling with the full system Jacobian. The answer acknowledges additional bifurcation classification work, but its initial diagnostic inference lacks the needed system-specific conditions.

evidence.title: GetFEM, Numerical continuation and bifurcation
evidence.finding: A bifurcation is defined by distinct solution curves through the same point, with separate detection and branching procedures. Jacobian singularity is a diagnostic, not by itself a classification.

F(u,lambda)=u^3+lambda^2*u=0 has the unique real solution u=0 for every lambda, while F_u=0 at (0,0). The solution set is still the single smooth branch u=0; Jacobian singularity alone does not imply an additional real branch.

The original says a standard Newton step fails at the bifurcation point, not that every run approaching a singular root inevitably fails. The hold concerns the unsupported singular-coupling-to-bifurcation inference.
